notes.comment:
This line applies the derive macros Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize to the SessionInfo struct. Debug enables pretty-printing for logging. Clone allows cheap copies. Serialize/Deserialize let serde automatically convert SessionInfo to/from JSON in .lines.json — the #[serde(rename = "sessionId")] on the field below maps session_id to the camelCase JSON key.
SessionInfo is persisted inside LinesFile and sent over the HTTP API, so it needs both Serialize (for writing to .lines.json and HTTP responses) and Deserialize (for reading back). Clone is used when the GUI reads the persisted session on startup. Debug is for developer convenience.

notes.comment: nice, could you give me more details?

handle_get_notes is the GET /session-api/notes endpoint. It loads .lines.json from disk via notes_store::load(), serializes the entire LinesFile struct (version, revision, session, notes) to JSON using serde_json::to_value, and returns it as the HTTP response body. If serialization fails it returns an error JSON. This is the primary endpoint AI CLIs call to fetch all user review notes.
This is a read-only endpoint — it does not modify .lines.json. The response includes the full LinesFile structure so AI agents can see both the notes and the session metadata (sessionId, cli, serverUrl) in one request. The revision counter in the response can be used for polling to detect changes.

However, the registered session in lazygitrs is antigravity-session-001 (cli: antigravity) — that was registered by the antigravity CLI before the conflict check was added. I cannot overwrite it now because the new register handler refuses to clobber an existing session. To switch to my session, you would need to unregister first: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:47657/session-api -H content-type: application/json --data {"action":"unregister"}, then register my session with force: true. The line you highlighted (246) is the conflict-check code I just added — it compares the existing session ID with the new one and returns status: conflict if they differ and force is not set.
The session conflict protection works as intended: antigravity registered first, and now opencode cannot overwrite it without force or unregister. This prevents AI CLIs from stepping on each other.

notes.comment:
This line explains that the registration step is where you tell lazygitrs which notification architecture to use. There are 3 options: (1) HTTP Push via serverUrl — best for opencode, which runs a local server on port 4096. lazygitrs POSTs directly to /tui/append-prompt + /tui/submit-prompt, injecting the prompt inline into the running TUI session. (2) SSE — AI CLIs connect to GET /session-api/events and receive real-time push events when notes are sent. Best for custom scripts or IDE extensions. (3) Spawn fallback — if no serverUrl and no SSE clients, lazygitrs spawns the configured notifyCommand as a subprocess. You choose by including serverUrl in your register call (for HTTP push), or omitting it (for SSE/spawn).
The registration step is the single entry point for AI CLIs to declare how they want to receive notifications. The serverUrl field triggers HTTP push mode; its absence triggers SSE/spawn mode.
notes.rationale: The registration step is the single entry point for AI CLIs to declare how they want to receive notifications. The serverUrl field triggers HTTP push mode; its absence triggers SSE/spawn mode.

notes.comment:
This line documents the new metadata fields added to our persistent note storage.
Before our work, `.lines.json` only stored the comment text and line number. We enriched it so that `lazygitrs` can distinguish between user notes and AI notes (`source`), display nice labels (`author`), and track the workflow state (`status` being New, Sent, or Addressed). The `revision` counter was added to prevent race conditions by keeping track of the file's generation.
